title: Adaptive KV precision controller and offline calibration harness
creator: Ana Varela
description:
Background: We need a production-friendly way to get the latency benefits of INT8/FP8 KV cache quantization without unacceptable quality regressions across workloads and sequence-length distributions. Previous one-size-fits-all profiles produced either good quality with limited cost savings or large speedups with tail regressions.

Objective: Implement an Adaptive KV Precision Controller (APC) plus an offline calibration harness (SampleBank) that together: 1) choose precision per-request or per-shard (INT8/FP8/FP16) based on runtime signals, 2) maintain a small per-model calibration bank for fast re-calibration on rollout, and 3) provide automated validation against our quality suites.

Hypothesis: A dynamic controller that factors in sequence length, KV cache hit ratio, recent token-level perplexity proxy, and model variant will recover >85% of INT8 latency gains while keeping end-user QA/accuracy regressions below 1.5% absolute on targeted benchmarks.

Scope: APC implementation in runtime routing layer, integration with KV execution engine (fast switch), SampleBank offline calibration tools (collect, calibrate, validate), CI checks that run a subset of calibration and quality tests at canary deploy. Does NOT include UI surface for the console (follow-up).

Experiment Plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): Implement controller hooks and a lightweight runtime policy evaluator. Add fast switch paths in KV executor for INT8/FP8/FP16. Build SampleBank tool to capture representative prefixes and calibration artifacts (per-layer scales, clipping params).
- Phase 2 (calib): Run automated calibration sweep for 3 representative models (redwood-7b, open-13b, community-65b) on 2 hardware targets (A100-40G, H100-80G). Store calibration profiles keyed by model+hardware+seq-dist.
- Phase 3 (validation): Evaluate on LAMBADA, TruthfulQA (subset), and internal SLO prompts (chat snippets). Measure quality deltas, token throughput, p50/p95 latency.
- Phase 4 (canary): Roll out APC as opt-in for select tenants with telemetry and automatic rollback based on quality gates.

Metrics / Acceptance Criteria:
- Latency: Achieve >=15% median token latency reduction vs baseline FP16 on at least two models when APC selects INT8/FP8.
- Quality: End-to-end QA accuracy drop <=1.5% absolute on LAMBADA and <=2% on in-house chat tests.
- Stability: No increase in error rate (exceptions/NaNs) at scale across 100k requests during canary.
- Operational: Calibration pipeline can produce a profile in <30 minutes for a model/hardware pair and profile size <1MB compressed.

Risks and Mitigations:
- Risk: Layerwise outliers cause catastrophic drift in tail queries. Mitigation: APC includes per-layer rollback threshold and immediate fallback to FP16 on token-level perplexity spike.
- Risk: Calibration overfits to sample bank and does not generalize. Mitigation: SampleBank will mix synthetic perturbations and real user prefixes; keep holdout calibration set.
- Risk: Runtime switching overhead negates gains. Mitigation: Benchmark switch cost; implement switch via single-instruction kernel selection path and cache last-used profile per worker.

Acceptance tests / CI gates:
- Unit tests for controller policy logic and profile lookup caching.
- Integration test that runs calibration on a tiny sample, loads profile, and runs 500 synthetic requests verifying latency and agreement metrics.
- Canary validation job with 10k requests against production-like traffic and automatic rollback if quality gate fails.

Deliverables:
- Runtime PR adding APC hook and fast precision switch paths.
- SampleBank repository with reproducible calibration runs and validation reports.
- Canary runbook and quality gating thresholds documented in Confluence.

Notes on implementation details: APC decision features: sequence_length, kv_hit_ratio, recent_token_entropy_estimate, model_variant, hardware_type. Decision policy starts as rule-based (thresholds tuned from bench) and will log telemetry for future ML-based policy. SampleBank calibration stores per-layer scale and zero-point candidates, per-head clipping stats, and a confidence score for each layer to enable partial mixed-precision (e.g., top-k layers in FP16, rest INT8).
comments: 2026-03-10 Ana Varela: Created ticket, sketched high-level design. Spoke with runtime owners about feasibility of fast switch; they flagged that current kernel selector does per-invocation dispatch which might add 0.3-0.6ms — need microbenchmarks.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Implemented a prototype policy evaluator and microbench harness. Early microbench: switch overhead ~0.45ms on A100 when switch path uses nvrtc kernels; when using precompiled kernels with pointer swap overhead drops to ~0.08ms. Will pursue precompiled path.

2026-03-11 Grace Patel (ML): Ran preliminary calibration sweep for redwood-7b on H100. INT8 profile reduced KV memory by 46% and increased throughput 20% for seq=512, but LAMBADA accuracy dropped 2.4% absolute; investigating per-layer fixes.

2026-03-12 Liam Chen: Added per-layer confidence mask to SampleBank; re-running sweep with top-3 layers forced FP16 yields LAMBADA drop 0.9% and throughput still +12% vs FP16 baseline. Good tradeoff candidate.
2026-03-12 Product note: PM Simon Owens - happy with mixed-precision approach as default safe mode; requested a canary plan and customer opt-in toggle.
